Article Title: 'New Parliament, PM house, why not new govt schools in villages?' CJP's Dipke announces nationwide campaign
Article Text:
CJP announces nationwide campaign to improve government schools on August 15.

The ‘Sarpanch Challenge’

CJP backs Jharkhand protests

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages, seeking to address the "neglect of rural educational infrastructure".The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to work together to improve basic facilities in government schools.Dipke said he would launch the initiative from his village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, by approaching the village head and requesting him to take steps to improve government schools there.“The coming 15th August is our 80th Independence Day. But, if anything has been neglected or ignored the most in the last 80 years, it is the government schools in our villages,” Dipke said on Monday.“We have made a new Parliament, a new PM house. Why have we not been able to build new schools in our villages? Do we not consider the children of farmers and labourers the future of our country?” he asked.Dipke said children in villages continue to face difficulties in accessing schools and basic facilities such as drinking water and toilets.“Even today, village children have to walk a long distance to go to school. After going there, they don’t find water or toilet facilities,” he said, highlighting the difficulties faced by girls in particular.“I feel that on this 15th August, if we should pay attention to anything, if we should make a new start, we should start by improving our government schools,” he said.As part of the campaign, the CJP has appealed to sarpanches across the country to take up the task of improving government schools in their respective villages.Dipke said he would personally approach the village head in Hingoli and urged other sarpanches to do the same in their villages.The organisation has termed the initiative the “Sarpanch Challenge”, under which it plans to publicly recognise village heads who improve their schools by sharing before-and-after photographs on its social media platforms and giving credit to the sarpanches concerned.“We will give you credit so that after seeing you, after seeing the schools that you have improved, many other village heads also start improving schools in their villages," Dipke said.The CJP has also called for a citizen-led social audit of government schools.Parents whose children study in government schools have been asked to visit the institutions and check basic facilities, including electricity, clean drinking water, functional washrooms and mid-day meals.“You go to your children's schools and see if basic facilities are available. See if there is electricity, water… Do your children get washroom facilities? Do they get mid-day meals?” Dipke said.He urged parents to record videos if basic facilities were unavailable. The CJP said it would soon issue a printable audit form through which citizens could record the facilities available at their children's schools and those that were missing.The form will be shared through links on campaign videos on the CJP's official social media platforms and completed forms and video evidence can be emailed to the organisation.The campaign aims to ensure that children of farmers and wage labourers studying in village schools have access to facilities comparable to those available to children in cities.“If not, you make videos of it. Because your children's schooling should be good. That is your fundamental right," Dipke said.“Let us all make a promise to the children who live in villages that we will improve their schools. Together, we can do this,” he said, concluding his video with the message, “Real India lives in villages”.In a separate video, Dipke also extended his support to Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was hospitalised after his health deteriorated during a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.Calling the alleged police action against protesters “cruel and inhuman”, Dipke drew a parallel with student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. “Be it Jantar Mantar or Jharkhand, such police brutality against students is cruel and inhuman,” he said.“CJP stands firmly with Devendra bhai and his struggle. He is a true hero. We salute his courage and strength!” he added.Mahto has been at the centre of the ongoing JPSC-JSSC agitation in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike and joined the students' Vidhan Sabha gherao march on Monday, arriving at the protest in an ambulance as his health deteriorated.The CJP, which began as an online satirical platform, later took its campaign to the streets. Its 36-day agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against examination irregularities was called off on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages. The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to improve basic facilities in government schools.

Article Title: Sharad Pawar’s MPs to meet PM Modi; Congress asks them to delink women’s quota, delimitation
Article Text:
NCP(SP) to meet PM Modi, delegation to raise issues affecting Maharashtra,.

NCP (SP) MPs to raise Maharashtra issues

NEW DELHI: A delegation of eight MPs from Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) is scheduled to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.Ahead of the meeting, the Congress has urged its alliance partner to convey the INDIA bloc's opposition to linking the implementation of women's reservation with the proposed delimitation exercise.AICC secretary Sachin Sawant urged the NCP (SP) delegation to press Modi for the immediate implementation of the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, without waiting for delimitation."It is learnt that the MPs of the Nationalist Congress Party - Sharadchandra Pawar will be meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday regarding issues concerning Maharashtra. We urge them to firmly convey to Prime Minister Modi that the INDIA Alliance's unequivocal position is that the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023, must be implemented immediately and should not be linked to delimitation," Sawant posted on X on Sunday."It is important that the unity of the INDIA Alliance and its opposition to the Modi government on this issue is made unequivocally clear," he added.The Congress' appeal comes ahead of the meeting between PM Modi and eight NCP (SP) MPs, led by party MP Supriya Sule.Sule had said on Saturday that the delegation would raise issues affecting Maharashtra, including farmer suicides, the water crisis and problems caused by rapid urbanisation."We - some MPs and I - were talking about that Prime Minister must be apprised about the problems in Maharashtra. There is water related issues, farmer suicides, and problems being faced due to urbanisation," Sule said at a press conference in Mumbai.BJP leader Navneet Rana welcomed the proposed meeting, saying elected representatives should be able to raise issues concerning Maharashtra's development with the Prime Minister."I feel that if MPs from Sharad Pawar 's party are meeting PM Modi for the sake of Maharashtra's development--driven by the belief that the state needs to progress further--then such a meeting is certainly not a bad thing," Rana said."While all sorts of speculations are being made, I believe any such speculation ultimately bodes well for Maharashtra; there could be nothing better than them approaching the PM to advocate for the state's development," she added.The dispute centres on the government's proposed delimitation exercise and its connection with the implementation of the women's reservation law. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposed increasing the strength of the House to 850 seats and sought to expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Act passed in 2023.The bill, however, failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed during the extended Budget Session.The Congress and other opposition parties have backed women's reservation but oppose making its implementation dependent on delimitation. They have argued that the reservation provisions should be implemented immediately rather than waiting for the expansion and redrawing of Lok Sabha constituencies.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) MPs to meet PM Modi, delegation to raise issues affecting Maharashtra. Congress has urged its alliance partner to convey the INDIA bloc's opposition to linking the implementation of women's reservation with the proposed delimitation exercise. AICC secretary Sachin Sawant urged the NCP delegation to press Modi for the immediate implementation of the Women's Reservation Act, passed in 2023.

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched a probe into irregularities in several recruitment exams in Jharkhand, including the JSSC-CGL exam, as news agency PTI quoted officials saying on Monday.The agency has taken note of an FIR filed by the state police CID and other complaints and will investigate the matter under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).The development comes as students have been protesting for 16 days, demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment exams, particularly the JSSC-CGL (Jharkhand General Graduate Level Combined Competitive Examination).The protests in Jharkhand has entered its 17th day on Monday.The students have refused to end their protest. The agitated students have started their march to "ghero" assembly, despite the government claiming it has accepted "98 per cent of the demands".However, the protesters has rejected Hemant Soren-led government's claims of "98% demands met," saying that only "3 out of 13 exams were cancelled."Meanwhile, the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) saw a major change on Sunday, with all three of its members resigning. The members are Ajeeta Bhattacharya, wife of JMM leader Supriyo Bhattacharyya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmad.Their resignations came after the Jharkhand CID summoned them for questioning over alleged irregularities, including paper leaks.

The agency has taken note of an FIR filed by the state police CID and other complaints. The development comes as students have been protesting for 16 days, demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment exams.

Article Title: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government
Article Text:
Both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA, pending investigation.

Air India pilots grounded till probe is over

NEW DELHI: The captain of Air India’s August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight, which experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet, was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival, whose result was “not negative” and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said Sunday.TOI had exclusively reported on Sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.The ministry has classified the incident, which led to 17 people being hospitalised, as serious and said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will probe it.“Further action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,” it said.Directorate General of Civil Aviation rules stipulate that “in case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety-sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received. In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisation” for de-addiction.Multiple passengers and cabin crew members on board the Airbus A320 operating as AI 2379 were injured when it suddenly lost altitude. The plane later landed safely in Delhi. “As standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing. Samples have been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,” the ministry statement added.Both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA, pending investigation.
Article Summary: The captain of Air India’s August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival. The result was “not negative” and has been sent for confirmatory tests. ToI had exclusively reported on Sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.

Article Title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
Article Text:
After bringing all crew members into the ‘citadel’, the master of the Golden Arsenal sought help from the Indian Navy, which responded swiftly to the distress call (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: On July 1, an attack by pirates on an India-bound bulk carrier, Golden Arsenal, in the Gulf of Aden was foiled after the captain moved all crew members, including an Indian seafarer, into the vessel’s “citadel” and sought assistance from the Indian Navy A citadel is a fortified safe room with essential supplies such as food and water, as well as communication equipment, where crew members can take refuge during a pirate attack. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel.Sharing this incident at the National Port Security Conference this week, Captain Vikram Singh Manhas, deputy nautical adviser at DGMA (maritime regulator), urged all crew members and masters to remain vigilant and follow preventive measures prescribed under best management practices (BMP), amid a rise in piracy incidents.Four vessels are held hostage by Somali pirates at present, three of which have Indian crew members aboard.One of the vessels has one Indian seafarer, while the other two have five and 11 Indian crew, respectively.Highlighting the significance of prevention in such cases, Manhas said that once a vessel is held by pirates, everything is dependent upon the negotiations with the pirates and that the government is working to ensure the safe release of Indian seafarers.In the direction of ensuring their safety, the government is set to launch a dashboard on August 15 to track every Indian seafarer on any ship. Additionally, shipping and ports minister Sarbananda Sonowal Saturday launched e-Samudra, a digital platform integrating services for seafarers, shipping companies, ports and other maritime stakeholders, and said, “Every Indian seafarer must be safe, respected and supported as India strengthens its position as a global maritime power. ”
Article Summary: On July 1, an attack by pirates on an India-bound bulk carrier, Golden Arsenal, in the Gulf of Aden was foiled. The captain moved all crew members, including an Indian seafarer, into the vessel’s ‘citadel’ and sought assistance from the Indian Navy. A citadel is a fortified safe room with essential supplies such as food and water, as well as communication equipment.

Article Title: Safari in snow leopard home? Conservationists say Ladakh is no Kaziranga
Article Text:
Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A safari car can roll past a rhino in Kaziranga. In Ranthambore, it can track a tiger. Put that car in Ladakh. For its elusive snow leopards — masters of camouflage in a landscape where survival depends on staying unseen — the question is whether tourism can get close enough to see them without making them disappear for good.Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails, triggering warnings from conservationists that turning a fragile high-altitude wilderness into a tourist circuit could disturb wildlife, commercialise off-roading and open the door to roads, eateries and other tourism infrastructure.“You cannot see a snow leopard from a jeep unless you do something illegal like placing bait or a sheep to lure it,” said Dr MK Ranjitsinh, emeritus member of Wildlife Trust of India, who has spent nearly 50 years shaping conservation strategies and played a key role in framing the Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972 and Project Tiger.“Kaziranga is not Ladakh and Ranthambore is not Ladakh. The ecology is completely different,” he added.In Ladakh’s open valleys, vehicles can be visible from miles away. Vegetation is concentrated along valley bottoms, drawing animals there to feed and drink. “Are you taking a safari there?” he asked.Ladakh is home to 477 of India’s estimated 718 snow leopards — the country’s largest population. It also supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species.But spotting a snow leopard is a needle-in-a-haystack affair. Its thick, mottled coat melts into rocky slopes, while steep, remote terrain gives it a vast natural advantage.The Ladakh govt spokesperson said lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena has directed the forest department to introduce guided safaris modelled on national parks such as Kaziranga and Ranthambore, using specially designed open-back vehicles operated by trained local drivers and guides. According to govt, the move is aimed at preventing illegal off-roading and disturbance of wildlife.The plan was cleared at the first governing body meeting of Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation Society, chaired by Saxena. Forest officials have been asked to explore routes across Hemis national park, Changthang and Karakoram wildlife sanctuaries, besides Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass.Ranjitsinh fears a different road ahead. “Wildlife safari may be good in principle but in practice it could be a disaster,” he said, warning that tourism and hotel lobbies could eventually overwhelm govt controls. “There will be demands for more roads, eating places and other infrastructure. Eventually, the whole landscape could turn into a festival.”A wildlife official said safaris work best where animals occur in large concentrations or herds — unlike Himalayan and Trans-Himalayan terrain. Ladakh already has roads across its protected areas, with tourist vehicles accessing most zones except some restricted border regions.“What they actually plan is to regularise and commercialise off-roading,” the official said, warning that vehicles could be allowed into fragile meadows for a price.Kaziranga and Ranthambore were built into India’s safari imagination. Ladakh’s proposed safari would venture into an entirely different world. Its snow leopards are scattered across an unforgiving landscape where the first rule of spotting one is knowing where not to look.
Article Summary: Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails. Conservationists warn that turning a fragile high- altitude wilderness into a tourist circuit could disturb wildlife, commercialise off-roading and open the door to roads.

Article Title: Air India turbulence scare: Airbus and French agency to join probe into Phuket flight
Article Text:
The aircraft plunged 300ft, injuring many on board

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: European aerospace major Airbus and France's Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety will join the probe to establish what caused the Air India A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi with 145 aboard to suddenly lose altitude by about 300ft last week, injuring many on board.Led by India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), the investigation is examining the twin aspects of the aircraft's mechanical issues and pilot behaviour. Everyone TOI spoke to said what happened mid-flight was indeed "a close shave". Luckily, the aircraft (AI 2379) landed safely at its destination, but 17 people had to be hospitalised.The captain's psychoactive substance screening test was not negative, and the confirmatory test result is not yet officially known. His behaviour on board is under the scanner. "One of the pilots fell in the cockpit and had to be assisted by cabin crew to get back on his seat," said a source. The flight data recorder will reveal mechanical failures, if any, and the cockpit voice recorder will reveal what transpired on the flight deck."Airbus is sending its team to India, and they will reach by Wednesday to inspect the aircraft and work with Air India and AAIB.Being a serious incident, the investigator of the original equipment manufacturer's country (France in this case) is also coming," said a source. An Airbus official said it is "providing technical assistance to the investigating authorities. We are actively supporting the airline and will provide further information as it becomes available".Industry executives said the A320 (VT-EXO) may have suffered a triple hydraulic failure for a few seconds, which is rare. This system uses a fluid under pressure to drive machinery or move mechanical components to power critical elements like wheel brakes, nose wheel steering, landing gear retraction/extension and flight control surfaces. It is also learnt the autopilot became disengaged during that tumultuous time for a few seconds, and the aircraft even got a stall warning.A pilot then steadied the aircraft by pushing the nose down.AI said it can't "comment on any findings or observations related to the investigation" as it "is being conducted by AAIB" and that the airline "will continue to extend our full cooperation to authorities as required". The flight data recorder will reveal the timestamps of the sequence of events - whether the alleged transient hydraulic failure occurred because of the aircraft's rapid descent or whether the aircraft first entered an air pocket and subsequent turbulence caused hydraulic failure.
Article Summary: Airbus and France's Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety will join the probe. The Air India A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi with 145 aboard suddenly lost altitude by about 300ft last week. The aircraft landed safely at its destination, but 17 people had to be hospitalised.

Article Title: Govt hints at JPC for FCRA Bill, opposition demands total rollback

NEW DELHI: Discussion on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2011 (FCRA) 2026, did not figure Monday in the business advisory committee (BAC) deliberations involving govt and different parties over Lok Sabha’s agenda for the remaining three days of the monsoon session, deepening uncertainty over whether the governing alliance will push for passage of the contentious legislation.Govt is said to have reached out to the Congress-led opposition seeking its views on referring the FCRA bill to a joint committee of Parliament for scrutiny.Sources said Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla spoke with Congress member of Parliament KC Venugopal regarding the govt’s proposal, but he instead sought complete withdrawal of the legislation.Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill was introduced on March 25 in Lok Sabha’s last session but has not been taken up for discussion yet amid sharp protests from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.Govt sources said they are looking at allaying their concerns, insisting that the apprehensions of Christian groups are ill-founded as the bill is religion-neutral. “Moreover, they receive less than 17% of funding under FCRA. Article Title: Number of govt elementary schools down 10,000 in a year
Article Text:
Data showed the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The number of govt elementary schools across the country fell by nearly 10,000 in a year, with Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recording the steepest declines, according to data tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday.UDISE+ data showed that the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26 - a reduction of 9,866 schools, or about 1.1%.The govt data was provided in response to a question from DMK MP T R Baalu on whether a large number of elementary schools had been closed because of insufficient student strength and the steps being taken to prevent dropouts. However, the education ministry did not specify how many of the schools were actually closed due to lack of students, while furnishing the overall number of govt elementary schools in the two academic years.Meghalaya recorded the biggest numerical decline, with the number of govt elementary schools falling from 7,633 to 5,459, a drop of 2,174. Telangana followed with a reduction of 1,961 schools, from 22,983 to 21,022, while Andhra Pradesh saw its count decline by 1,446, from 37,449 to 36,003.Madhya Pradesh had 1,043 fewer schools, Karnataka 615, West Bengal 587, Rajasthan 473 and Maharashtra 357. Himachal Pradesh recorded a decline of 259 schools, while Assam had 209 fewer.Uttar Pradesh, which continues to have the largest network of govt elementary schools, saw the number fall marginally from 1,34,115 to 1,33,948.Not every state recorded a decline. Bihar's count rose from 66,803 to 66,915, while Chhattisgarh increased from 43,836 to 43,853. The numbers remained unchanged in Jammu & Kashmir, Puducherry and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.The ministry said opening, closing and rationalisation of schools fall within the jurisdiction of state and UT govts since education is on the Concurrent List.At the same time, it said access to schooling had improved. The Gross Access Ratio rose between 2018-19 and 2025-26 from 96.49 to 98.14 at upper-primary level, from 88.24 to 95.05 at secondary level and from 65.05 to 94.79 at higher-secondary level.The Centre said states were being supported through Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN, besides assistance for school infrastructure, residential schools and hostels, transport facilities, enrolment drives, textbooks and uniforms to curb dropouts and improve enrolment.
Article Summary: Number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26. Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recorded the steepest declines.

Article Title: CM defends FCRA amendments, rejects ‘anti-Christian’ charge
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagpur: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday defended proposed amendments to Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), alleging that a section of organizations receiving foreign funds had used the money for "anti-national activities" and that the changes were intended to curb such misuse rather than target any particular community.Responding to criticism from Congress, which has described the proposed amendments as "anti-Christian", he said FCRA framework applies uniformly to every organisation receiving foreign contributions, irrespective of religion or community."The reason for bringing the FCRA amendments is that some organisations have been bringing foreign money into the country and using it for anti-national activities. That has to stop," Fadnavis said."Those who are doing good work have nothing to worry about. There will be an FCRA mechanism and their licences will be protected," he said.Rejecting the allegation that the amendments specifically target Christian organizations, Fadnavis said the law governs all entities receiving foreign donations."This is not a question of one community. It is applicable to every organization that receives foreign donations, irrespective of its community," he said.Fadnavis said anyone with reservations about the proposed legislation should raise them during the parliamentary process, adding that Union govt was open to hearing different views."I believe that if anyone has objections, they should raise them in Parliament. The govt of India is receptive," he said.Referring to statements made in the United States on the proposed amendments, Fadnavis questioned why individuals outside India were reacting to the legislation."Some people in the US have commented on the FCRA Amendment Bill. What does that mean? The very purpose of these amendments becomes clear from such reactions," he said, without elaborating further.The CM reiterated that the objective of the proposed amendments was to ensure accountability in the use of foreign contributions and prevent their misuse, while protecting organizations carrying out lawful activities.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis defends proposed amendments to Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) He says FCRA framework applies uniformly to every organisation receiving foreign contributions, irrespective of religion or community. Congress has described the proposed amendments as "anti-Christian"

Article Title: Navy chief on 4-day visit to Mauritius to boost maritime cooperation

Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan begins four-day Mauritius visit

NEW DELHI: Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan on Monday went to Mauritius on a four-day official visit to strengthen bilateral maritime cooperation.The visit is part of India's continued engagement to defence ties with Mauritius, an extremely valued partner in the Indian Ocean Region.During the visit, the Navy chief will interact with the senior leadership of the govt of Mauritius and hold discussions on matters of mutual interest such as maritime security, defence cooperation, capacity building and military collaboration, the Navy said in a statement.Such engagements are aimed at strengthening Indo-Mauritius cooperation in the maritime domain, enhancing operational-level linkages and consolidating the robust strategic partnership between India and Mauritius, it said.The visit of Admiral Swaminathan to Mauritius after assuming charge as the Navy chief underscores the priority India accords to the friendship it shares with Mauritius, anchored in mutual respect, trust and a shared commitment to maritime security, regional cooperation and stability in the Indian Ocean Region.India and Mauritius share a close and enduring maritime partnership.Indian Navy engages regularly with the National Coast Guard through training exchanges, operational interactions including joint exclusive economic zone surveillance, port visits and hydrographic surveys.Both countries also participate and engage with each other in multilateral forums and cooperative initiatives.Mauritius has been a regular participant in key Indian Navy initiatives such as Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, MILAN, International Fleet Review, Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR and Exercise AIKEYME, aptly reflecting the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) they share.

NEW DELHI: The government has notified 11 more international ports in the country, including 9 land ports and 2 airports, for the entry of eligible foreigners arriving on electronic visas (e-visas). They can now land with e-visa at Bhopal and Tirupati airports and clear immigration.The additional landports via which e-visa holding foreign nationals can enter India include Attari in Punjab; Gede, Ghojanga and Jaigaon in West Bengal; Darranga in Assam; Agartala in Tripura; Moreh in Manipur; and Haridaspur in Odisha.E-visas currently make up 78% of the total visas issued in the country. Having taken off with 43 eligible countries, the facility is now available to nationals of 172 countries.E-visa is presently issued under 17 sub-categories; namely tourist visa, mountaineering visa, business visa (six types), medical visa (four types), student visa (two types), transit visa, miscellaneous visa and group visitor visa (cruise).

Article Title: 'US has similar laws': Indian envoy Vinay Kwatra clarifies FCRA Bill, shares 'myth vs reality' check
Article Text:
Kwatra issued a “Myth vs. Reality check” on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill.

‘FCRA does not target any religion’

‘Foreign money inflows have been rising’

‘US has FARA, FATCA’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Monday defended the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), saying the changes are aimed at improving transparency, governance and oversight of foreign funds.In a series of posts on X on Monday, Kwatra issued a “Myth vs. Reality check” on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, amid concerns raised by sections of civil society and a US lawmaker over the legislation.Kwatra said regulating foreign financial flows in public and political spaces was a sovereign measure driven by national security concerns and was common in several democracies.“Truth: Regulation of foreign financial flows in public and political spaces is a sovereign step driven by national security concerns. It is an accepted feature of modern governance in many democracies around the world,” he said.Responding to the claim that India was framing a new law to cut off foreign aid to civil society, Kwatra said the proposed legislation did not prohibit Indians from receiving foreign donations or seek to shut down law-abiding organisations.“The fact is that the law does not forbid Indians from receiving foreign donations or shut down law abiding civil society.Tens of thousands of associations are registered under FCRA and routinely receive foreign funds for health, education, disaster relief, research and humanitarian work,” he said.Kwatra said the FCRA was first enacted in India in 1976 and replaced by a new framework in 2010. It was subsequently strengthened through amendments in 2016, 2018 and 2020.“The 2026 Bill and Rules are the next step in the same direction: more transparency, better governance, clearer rules,” he said.Kwatra also rejected allegations that the FCRA amendments "specifically target a particular religion or community."“Truth: Nothing could be farther from it. The Act applies uniformly to all organisations regardless of religion, community or ideology,” he said.He added that faith-based welfare activities, including religious education, maintenance of places of worship and charitable work by organisations of all faiths, would continue to be eligible for foreign funding.Kwatra also rejected claims that the FCRA had adversely affected NGOs and charitable organisations or that the proposed amendments would further restrict their operations.“Truth: In reality, foreign money inflows into India have been rising, not falling. Foreign contributions to registered organisations grew from roughly $1.2 billion in 2010–11 to $2.67 billion in 2024–25,” he said.He said India has more than 3 million NGOs, while only 14,450 have FCRA registration, arguing that the overwhelming majority of civil society organisations fall outside the ambit of the Act.“FCRA does not stop anyone from accepting foreign charity, research grants or humanitarian aid. It asks three things — register, receive the money through laid down process, report what you did with it,” Kwatra said.Addressing concerns that the proposed law would allow the government to seize assets of NGOs, religious charities, places of worship, hospitals and schools dependent on foreign donations, Kwatra said the provision regarding assets was not new.“When a registration is cancelled or surrendered, foreign contributions and the assets created from them already vest in a State Government authority. This has been in force since 2010. It is not new,” he said.According to Kwatra, the 2026 Bill proposes to create a designated authority to safeguard such assets and also provides a mechanism for their return if an organisation restores its FCRA registration.“What the 2026 Bill adds is a designated authority to safeguard those assets — and a way back. If the organisation restores its registration, all assets and unused funds are returned in full,” he said.He also said the proposed legislation contains specific provisions for places of worship.“Places of worship carry their own protection. Where a cancelled association has created property connected to a place of worship, that property goes to another FCRA-registered association of the same faith to ensure continuity of worship,” Kwatra said.Kwatra also dismissed the argument that India was an outlier in regulating foreign funding, pointing to similar laws in other countries.“Truth: The US has had FARA since 1938 and FATCA since 2010. Australia legislated in 2018, Canada in 2024. The UK's scheme came into force in July 2025. The EU is legislating now,” he posted on X.His comments came days after a US lawmaker raised concerns over the proposed FCRA amendments, claiming that the legislation could allow the Indian government to take control of churches and charities.The FCRA Bill, 2026 proposes to empower the government to create a “Designated Authority” to take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such contributions when an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases because it is not renewed.The Bill also states that where such assets constitute a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is maintained.
Article Summary: India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra defended the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Kwatra issued a “Myth vs. Reality check” on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, amid concerns raised by sections of civil society.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday allowed TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for three weeks in September for eye treatment.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant allowed the travel but imposed several conditions.Banerjee can travel only on his diplomatic passport and will have to provide details of his travel itinerary, where he will stay abroad, the doctor and hospital where he will receive treatment, his accommodation and flight details.The court said investigating agencies can use the information provided by Banerjee for their investigation but must keep the details confidential.Banerjee had approached the Supreme Court challenging a Calcutta high court order that had refused to lift the travel restriction imposed on him in connection with a hate speech case.Earlier, the Calcutta high court had denied Banerjee permission to travel abroad for eye treatment after he refused to appear before a medical board at the state-run SSKM Hospital.Justice Saugata Bhattacharya had directed Banerjee to appear before the medical board on August 6.The board was supposed to examine his condition and inform the court whether he needed treatment abroad or whether the treatment could be provided in India.During the hearing, Justice Bhattacharya asked Banerjee's lawyer whether the TMC leader was willing to be examined by a medical board headed by the head of the Ophthalmology department at SSKM Hospital.Banerjee's lawyer, after taking instructions, said the TMC leader wanted to be examined by a doctor of his choice.However, Banerjee later informed the court that he was unwilling to appear before the medical board.The high court then dismissed his plea seeking permission to travel abroad.The court said an examination by the SSKM medical board was necessary to assess Banerjee's condition and help determine whether he needed treatment outside India.

NEW DELHI: Russian deputy PM Marat Khusnullin has suggested exploring a direct rail link from Moscow to the ‘Indian Ocean’ to avert risks associated with the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz, amid ongoing conflicts, including in West Asia, that have stalled the ambitious India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. Bosphorus is a narrow, natural strait in Turkey that connects Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.“A rail link to the Indian Ocean should also be explored. Risks related to the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz might require alternative routes: through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. Any options providing access to India are acceptable,” he told Russian news agency TASS.Experts said constructing a rail link spanning two continents and four countries would be a gigantic challenge. Apart from logistical difficulty and cost, for any option to extend the rail link to India, New Delhi would have to deal with the fact that it would pass through Pakistan, and a lot would depend on obtaining an iron-clad guarantee for securing cooperation and commitment of the hostile neighbour to protect the railway and cargo.The statement does not provide a detailed construction plan, cost estimate or timeline. However, if such a corridor is eventually developed, it could create a direct overland rail freight route linking Russia with India while offering an alternative to traditional maritime shipping routes.Among railway corridors linking multiple nations, Yiwu-Madrid is the longest freight train line in the world — spanning a little over 13,000 km, it connects China’s Yiwu to Spain’s Madrid, traversing eight countries.
Article Summary: Russian deputy PM Marat Khusnullin has suggested exploring a direct rail link from Moscow to the ‘Indian Ocean’ This would avert risks associated with the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz, amid ongoing conflicts, including in West Asia.

NEW DELHI: The captain operating Air India’s turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight on Tuesday (Aug 4) reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test conducted on arrival, according to multiple sources. The airline did not either confirm or deny it, saying while the tests were conducted, the results have not been shared with it.“We are aware that a post-flight screening test was conducted on the pilots in accordance with applicable protocols. However, the results of the test have not been shared with Air India, and we are therefore not in a position to comment on any findings,” an AI spokesperson said.“Air India undertakes regular drug testing of crew members in compliance with civil aviation regulations, independent of any specific flight or operational incident. We will continue to cooperate with the relevant authorities as required,” the airline added.The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. On arrival in Delhi, 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised. Sources say the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is probing this case from all angles including whether the handling of this turbulence event was correct; whether the event happened due to weather or some other reason; the likely impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.Pending probe, flight crew is taken off flying duty as per protocol. So the pilots of this flight are also not flying currently. DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such crew member can return for active duties with a negative dope test report.But after resuming flying if the same person tests positive for psychoactive substances again, their licence will be suspended for three years. And if after resuming flying the same person again tests positive for the third time, the flying licence is cancelled.International Civil Aviation Organisation says that “holders of licences shall not exercise the privileges of their licences and related ratings while under the influence of any psychoactive substance, which might render them unable to safely and properly exercise these privileges”.While the probe in Tuesday’s event would have focused on pilot handling the situation anyway, the captain reportedly testing positive adds another dimension to the same.
Article Summary: The captain operating Air India’s turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test. The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised.

NEW DELHI: Meta's platforms must comply with Indian law and cannot be governed solely by the company's global policies, news agency ANI reported quoting government sources said on Sunday.This follows a series of meetings between the social media giant and the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY). Officials also clarified that it would be factually incorrect to say the government had "directed Meta to completely overhaul its algorithm".The government’s focus, is on ensuring that Meta’s content policies, platform guidelines and moderation systems are aligned with Indian law. While concerns remain, officials said the discussions are aimed at securing concrete changes from the company rather than simply seeking assurances, ANI reported quoting sources.Sources told ANI that India's cultural context is not always fully understood by teams based outside the country. They said Meta needs greater local input, including stronger understanding of Indian languages and cultural nuances, to improve content moderation in India.The latest clarification came after a meeting on Friday between Meta's technical team and MeitY officials, during which the company explained its existing systems for handling harmful content online. Technical discussions between the two sides remain underway, with another round of meetings expected next week, sources said.On child sexual abuse material (CSAM), government sources told ANI that there is zero tolerance and zero compromise.Officials said allowing such material to remain on Meta's platforms would amount to a serious violation of rules. They said the company needs to adopt stronger and more proactive measures, with concrete action expected instead of assurances.The issue was also raised during earlier meetings between Meta's global team and government officials, amid wider concerns over the company's content moderation systems.The government has also raised concerns over deepfakes involving prominent personalities.Sources told ANI that content posted from authorised or verified handles should not be incorrectly identified as deepfakes. Officials said such sensitive cases cannot be left entirely to automated detection systems and called for a "human-in-the-loop" mechanism to ensure content is properly reviewed before any takedown.The government has also questioned Meta over synthetically generated content that reappears after being identified and removed as a deepfake.Officials have sought details from Meta on the concrete steps it is taking to prevent such content from resurfacing after removal.Meta's recommendation and virality algorithms have also come under scrutiny during the discussions.The government questioned why users are frequently shown content unrelated to their stated interests and whether this points to shortcomings in Meta's recommendation systems, ANI reported.Officials also asked why synthetically generated content continues to be amplified through the company's algorithms.The government has insisted that once such content is flagged, it should not be recommended further or repeatedly resurface on the platform, sources said.The issue of Meta's recommendation systems had also figured in earlier meetings with IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and senior ministry officials, when the company's global team was questioned about its algorithms and compliance with Indian laws.The latest discussions follow several rounds of engagement between Meta and the Indian government over deepfakes, CSAM, bot accounts, synthetic content and the company's compliance with Indian laws.According to earlier reports, Meta's technical team had explained its proposed measures to address the concerns raised by the government and said it had solutions to tackle deepfakes, CSAM and bot accounts.The government has also been examining Meta's compliance with intermediary provisions under Indian law, including the conditions governing safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act.The Centre had earlier sought action against deepfake content and was examining whether Meta's role in determining what content users see could have implications for its status as an intermediary.The latest discussions, however, have focused on the technical functioning of Meta's systems and how its global policies are implemented in India.As the talks continue, government sources said the objective is not to demand a complete overhaul of Meta's algorithm but to ensure that its platforms, content policies and moderation mechanisms comply with Indian law and adequately account for India's linguistic and cultural context.
Article Summary: Government sources say Meta's platforms must comply with Indian law. This follows a series of meetings between the social media giant and the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) Officials said the discussions are aimed at securing concrete changes from the company rather than simply seeking assurances.

Article Title: ED director Rahul Navin's tenure extended by a year
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Rahul Navin has been granted a one-year extension as ED director as his two-year fixed tenure was due to end this month.The tenure of Navin, a 1993-batch Indian Revenue Service (I-T) officer, as director of enforcement has been extended for a period of one year beyond "13.08.2026 i.e. up to 13.08.2027, including extension in service beyond the date of his superannuation or until further orders," as per DoPT.After three years as ED director, he could get two more extensions and serve till August 2029, all through the PM Modi government's tenure, with polls due in April-May 2029.Navin's tenure as director (in-charge) began on September 15, 2023, and he was appointed as ED director on August 14, 2024, while his service retirement was due on July 31, 2027. He has set a roadmap for officers to complete probes within two years and ensure attached properties are auctioned and restituted to rightful claimants and fraud victims, including banks or individuals.
Article Summary: Rahul Navin has been granted a one-year extension as ED director. His two-year fixed tenure was due to end this month. He could get two more extensions and serve till August 2029, with polls due in April-May 2029.

NEW DELHI: ED filed two chargesheets, one each against Reliance Communications (RCom) and Reliance Infrastructure Ltd, on Saturday before a special court here, naming Gautam Doshi, Sateesh Seth, Amitabh Jhunjhunwala and the two entities of Anil Ambani's Reliance Group as the accused for offences of money laundering and defalcation of bank funds of over Rs 40,000 crore.In its chargesheet against RCom, the agency has said that "the proceeds of crime are quantified at Rs 40,186 crore, the outstanding sum defaulted on by the entities to a consortium of banks and financial institutions".The role of the accused in the raising, deployment, concealment and projection of the funds, including false certification of end-use of $1 billion in FCCB proceeds, was also highlighted.ED sought confiscation of properties worth Rs 8,078 crore attached earlier in the case, belonging to Reliance Communications and its promoters and directors, including assets of Anil Ambani.The chargesheet against Reliance Infrastructure Ltd said, "Probe revealed an organised scheme to divert public funds from four NHAI-awarded toll-road projects: Trichy-Karur (NH-67), Trichy-Dindigul (NH-45), Salem-Ulundurpet (NH-68) and Jaipur-Reengus (NH-11).
